results.description: Financial reporters also tracked compute and infrastructure expense as a percentage of revenue—a ratio that fell from painful triple-digit territory in early 2025 to roughly 48% in the quarter ended June 30, 2026, before ticking up to 58% in the September quarter. Improving operating leverage is the bull case: if revenue scales faster than infra spending, percentages fall and free cash flow appears. The bear case is a demand air pocket: utilization drops, committed spend does not, and Anthropic burns balance sheet flexibility faster than the market reprices the stock. Investors on the roadshow reportedly pressed Amodei on how long Anthropic’s technical lead can last—not because Claude is weak today, but because open models, Google’s Gemini stack, OpenAI’s distribution, and Meta’s research pipelines compress differentiation cycles.
